cards.title: Python's four data structures
cards.purpose: Python has four built-in data structures. Today's is the set; the room has already met the list and the tuple.
cards.heading: Four data structures in Python
show: A data structure holds many values under one name.
Songs in order. A song can come twice.
Look up a name, get the number.

presses.screen: The line <q>A data structure holds many values under one name.</q> over four face-down tiles.
presses.say: We have met this word before. What is a data structure?
presses.room: Say it in your own words.

presses.screen: Tile 1 turns over: the picture <q>A playlist</q>, the name <q>list</q>, and the line <q>Songs in order. A song can come twice.</q> It gets a small tick: already learnt.
presses.say: We know this one. Ask the room for its line before you press.

presses.screen: Tile 2 turns over: the picture <q>Your date of birth</q>, the name <q>tuple</q>, and the line <q>Fixed. Nobody edits it.</q> It gets a small tick: already learnt.
presses.say: We know this one. Ask the room for its line before you press.

presses.screen: Tile 3 turns over: the picture <q>Seen by, on your story</q>, the name <q>set</q>, and the line <q>Each name once. No order.</q> It lights up and stays lit, marked <q>Today</q>.
presses.say: Before this tile turns: does the order matter here? Can one thing come twice? Then press.
presses.room: Hands up for yes, then for no, on each question.

presses.screen: Tile 4 turns over: the picture <q>Contacts</q>, the name <q>dictionary</q>, and the line <q>Look up a name, get the number.</q> It stays dim, marked <q>Later</q>.
presses.say: Name it only. It comes later.

must: All four tiles are on the card from press 1, face down, so nothing jumps.
Only the names and the everyday pictures. No code and no brackets for a structure not yet taught.
The set tile ends lit; earlier tiles keep their tick.

Draw it in the phone world: a playlist is a list, a date of birth is a tuple, Seen by is a set, Contacts is a dictionary. Do not take the picture further than this: the apps do far more than keep values; only the shape of the data carries over

cards.title: What a set is
cards.purpose: A set, in five lines: how it is written, whether it keeps order, whether it allows repeats, how you reach one item, and whether it can change. Set beside the ones already learnt.
cards.heading: What is a set?

presses.screen: A grid. Rows: <q>Written with</q>, <q>Keeps the order?</q>, <q>Same item twice?</q>, <q>Reach one item by</q>, <q>Can you change it?</q>. Columns: <q>list</q>, <q>tuple</q>, <q>set</q>. The earlier columns are filled; the set column is empty dashed cells.
presses.say: Here is what makes a set a set. One row at a time. Row 1 first.

presses.screen: Row 1, <q>Written with</q>: the set cell fills <q>{ }</q>. Beside it, small, the code that proves it and its output: <q><class 'set'></q>.
presses.say: Read the proof's output. Compare it with the tuple column. Next row: ask first.
presses.room: Hands up for yes, then for no, on the next row.

presses.screen: Row 2, <q>Keeps the order?</q>: the set cell fills <q>No</q>. Beside it, small, the code that proves it and its output: <q>{'Teja', 'Ravi', 'Sneha', 'Kiran', 'Anu'} / (run it again) / {'Anu', 'Kiran', 'Teja', 'Ravi', 'Sneha'}</q>.
presses.say: Read the proof's output. Compare it with the tuple column. Next row: ask first.
presses.room: Hands up for yes, then for no, on the next row.

presses.screen: Row 3, <q>Same item twice?</q>: the set cell fills <q>No</q>. Beside it, small, the code that proves it and its output: <q>2</q>.
presses.say: Read the proof's output. Compare it with the tuple column. Next row: ask first.
presses.room: Say the answer for the next row.

presses.screen: Row 4, <q>Reach one item by</q>: the set cell fills <q>No position. Ask with in</q>. Beside it, small, the code that proves it and its output: <q>True / TypeError: 'set' object is not subscriptable</q>.
presses.say: Read the proof's output. Compare it with the tuple column. Next row: ask first.
presses.room: Hands up for yes, then for no, on the next row.

presses.screen: Row 5, <q>Can you change it?</q>: the set cell fills <q>Yes</q>. Beside it, small, the code that proves it and its output: <q>3</q>.
presses.say: Read the proof's output. Compare it with the tuple column. That is a set.

cards.interaction: Before each row of today's column fills, the room says it or votes with hands. The proof's output decides.
must: The whole grid, row labels and empty cells, is on the card from press 1. One cell of today's column fills per press.
Earlier columns never change. The room reads today's cell against them.
Each filled cell keeps its proof beside it: the code and its exact output from data.proofs.
must_not: Fill a cell before the room has voted on it.
